questions.explanation: Passing command and arguments as separate parameters prevents shell injection vulnerabilities and ensures the execve system call correctly interprets the executable path and its argv array.

Cmd.Run() starts the command and immediately blocks waiting for its completion (equivalent to Start() followed by Wait()). Cmd.Start() non-blockingly launches the process, returning control immediately.

When a command is missing or execution fails, the shell should catch the specific error returned by the execution function (such as exec.ErrNotFound) and print a clean error message to standard error without crashing.
